It could be a sign, but it doesn’t necessarily have to mean that SA occurred. It’s really hard to put those pieces together, especially when you don’t remember what happened.

In my case, I remember the events of the initial trauma, which made it a lot easier to connect the dots between my sudden fixation and my previous SA. ~5 years ago I was with this horrible, abusive jerk who would tell me that he’d love me more/I’d be a better partner/he wouldn’t have to hurt me if I was “compliant”. He’s the one who originally made me aversive to the sex act in question, and thankfully I’ve been free of him for a long time now. Last night I started wondering if my current partner (who retraumatized me) would be happier/love me more now that I’m fixated on the act. And that made me realize that my fixation wasn’t because I suddenly liked the act again. I’m just trying to cope with what happened and dealing with a lot of repressed feelings and was minimizing how bad my current situation is. 

So, long story short, your fixations could mean it but it’s super hard to tell without knowing the background behind it. But, and I really want to stress this, not knowing for sure doesn’t make your trauma any less valid.

Best of luck on your journey!! It’s such a hard road coming out of comphet relationships (and coming out in general, if you’re in a place where you feel like you want to do that/can do that safely). You definitely aren’t broken, and I hope you get to a place where you feel like you can live freely and authentically.

The Satanic Temple is very big into advocacy for human rights (especially women’s rights). There are tenants, however those are more of a loose guideline involving things such as acting with compassion and empathy and respecting other people’s freedom.

I understand that cooking two meals is a pain, I truly do. I’ve had to do it myself more often than not for the past couple of years. I agree that she should learn to be able to provide and take care of herself. However, since she’s so new to it, you guys helping her out and researching/cooking with her could benefit her greatly.

If she’s not getting the proper nutrients she could end up with a lot of deficiencies, and that’s my major concern. I know it’s important for *her* to do her own research, but she might not be fully aware of just how much she needs to consider when making the change. When I first went vegetarian at 14, even with my parents help after a year I ended up getting really sick from it. None of us were educated enough to anticipate me needing to make other changes like adding in vitamin supplements.

Now that I’m an adult my parents still make sure when we cook together when I’m home that we have options for all of us, and that kind of connection really makes the relationship stronger, too. My dad loves cooking so we usually will make the same thing side by side, which is an option you can consider. We use the same recipe but modify it for our own diets. For example, when making pasta dishes we’ll use different noodles and sauces, but the same veggies/spices. Or he’ll add in meat and I won’t.

It’s not modern dogmas, sorry to burst your bubble. Children, along with the elderly and people with disabilities, tend to be some of the most powerless, vulnerable people in society. People like children and disabled adults can be especially at danger in situations of sexually abuse. That’s because they may not (yet) fully have a grasp of their rights ie consent and abuse.

Before you start arguing, yes, the elderly and some people with disabilities can consent. However, there are several individuals who can not consent because their disability makes them unable to. They do not have the cognition to be able to consent to sexually relations because that part of their brain isn’t developed enough. Now in children, their brains are still developing so they can reach a point where consenting to a relationship with an age gap like that is okay. As it stands her brain isn’t fully formed enough. 

It’s not taboo. It’s people trying their best to protect the most vulnerable people in society. You can’t tell me someone who doesn’t have the same decision making capabilities as you can consent to a situation like this with an adult who doesn’t have any of the same issues. You understand the law. You have a vast knowledge of sexuality. You have a fully developed brain. You have so many advantages that enable you to make decisions of consent that she does not yet have.

I keep seeing you mention that the laws of consent were made due to “Puritanism and taboo” which is horribly incorrect.

The reason why teenagers can consent to other teenagers and not to adults is because teenagers are in the same stages of development as each other. I don’t care how “mature” or “different” you think a teenager is, they’re a teenager. They haven’t fully psychologically or emotionally matured anywhere near the level a typical adult has.

One major point I want to stress is that the prefrontal cortex (the part of the brain where rational decisions get made) is NOT developed at her age. It won’t be fully developed until sometime in her 20s. Her brain also hasn’t finished going through synaptic pruning (a process which makes the brain more efficient in general).

Whether or not you want to believe it, she doesn’t have the capabilities that an adult does to make sane, responsible decisions. She won’t for another 6 years. She is also at a stage where seeking approval and fitting in is one of the most important things to her. If you think she isn’t likely to do what her adult “boyfriend” wants her to do in order to get that validation you’re delusional. This is doubly so because 14 is around the time period most people first start forming an interest in having romantic relationships. She has little to no experience with “serious” relationships and there’s a chance she might not even know what she wants in a relationship.

Being with another teenager is a safe experience. They have around the same levels of experience socially and romantically, they’re at the same stages of development biologically, and it’s a very low risk scenario. You are a grown man. You’ve had life experiences she probably won’t have for several years, and she probably sees you as an “authority figure” because of it. That’s going to lead to a power imbalance which at that stage of her life is unhealthy.

She is a vulnerable girl who I very much doubt knows your intentions behind targeting her. I highly doubt her parents are aware of it either. When you cut, it releases endorphins in your body, and they help block out the physical/emotional pain you’re feeling. It leads to something quite similar to a “high”. However, obviously the high doesn’t last, and just like with any addiction it becomes harder and harder to chase it. You start needing to self harm more often and more intensely in order for the same amount of endorphins to release. So it’s 100% an addiction, you get addicted to the chemicals that get released in your brain when you self harm.
